1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 g6 5..strategy: Defends e4 against the knight on f6 and adds a third guard of d5, which completes the clamp on Black's centre. Black's freeing ...d5 push is all but ruled out, so Black must look for counterplay elsewhere, in a slow manoeuvring game in which White keeps the extra space.

Trades off White's best-placed piece at once to ease the cramp. With no bishop on e3 yet, only the queen can recapture, and it is drawn to d4, where Black can try to gain time against it. White keeps the space, but Black develops freely.
